title: Class diagram and interfaces
idea: A class diagram shows each class, its public methods and how classes relate; interfaces mark the seams where one part can be swapped for another.
points: In an interview diagram, a box shows the class name, key fields and methods.
Arrows say how classes relate: has-a, uses, creates or implements.
`BookingService` depends on interfaces, never on a concrete database or rule.
JavaScript has no interfaces; a base class whose methods throw stands in.

edges.label: uses
edges.caption: The service asks the policy whether a slot clashes. It never knows which rule is plugged in.

edges.caption: Bookings are read and saved through an interface, so memory or a database both fit.

edges.caption: Room lookups go through their own repository: one interface per kind of data.

edges.caption: Telling attendees is a separate job, so the service only calls the notifier.

edges.label: creates
edges.caption: The service creates a `Booking` only after the policy says the slot is free.

edges.label: has many
edges.caption: Composition: a `Building` owns its rooms. A room does not exist outside one.

edges.label: refers to
edges.caption: A booking stores the room id, not a copy of the room.

code.title: Two policies, one interface
code.caption: Both classes honour the same contract, so `BookingService` can take either. Set the strict gap on line 9 to `0.25` and run again.

walk.text: The interface: a base class whose method throws until a subclass overrides it.
One overlap test with an optional gap, shared by both policies.
Two strategies. The buffer one adds a quarter hour between meetings for cleaning.
The same back-to-back request gets a different answer from each policy.

code.title: A missing method fails loudly
code.caption: The subclass forgot `forRoom`. The base class turns that gap into a clear error, not `undefined`.

pitfalls: Do not draw every private field; show the public methods others call.
Avoid an arrow from `BookingService` to a concrete class like an in-memory repository.
Keep interfaces small; split one that forces classes to stub unused methods.

options: TypeError: conflicts is not a function
quiz.why: `LenientPolicy` does not override `conflicts`, so the call finds the base method on the prototype chain, and it throws.

takeaway: Draw classes with public methods; depend on interfaces at every seam.
